Tom / team — reviewed the redlines. Proposed positions below (see attached redline .docx for precise text):

1) Governing law: Redwood's preference is New York (familiar bench for our CS/ops teams). We're willing to accept Delaware for enterprise deals only if reciprocated by a narrow equitable-relief carve.

2) Emergency relief carve: we can agree to limited injunctive relief in court prior to arbitration but only when narrowly tailored to:
   - protection of Redwood's trade secrets or ClearHarbor's confidential data,
   - prevention of ongoing exfiltration or misuse that would cause irreparable harm.
   - language must include an explicit requirement to seek expedited arbitration within 30 days of filing and a stay request once arbitration is underway.

3) Arbitration: final and binding in Delaware (for deals with Delaware governing law), AAA rules with confidentiality provisions.

4) If ClearHarbor insists on broad emergency relief (no arbitration stay), propose a middle ground: forum for emergency relief limited to courts in State of Delaware or federal courts in DE/NY with a six-week automatic stay for arbitration commencement.

Attachments: Redwood_Counter_redlines_MSAv1.docx

If that set is acceptable, we can finalize and get internal sign-offs. Laura

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Tom Riggins <legal@clearharbor.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:18:40 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines: governing law & emergency relief

Laura / Jasmine — appreciate the quick turn. Two points from our GC:

- Delaware is our starting point; they view its courts as predictable for commercial disputes. They will not accept New York for this agreement.
- The carve you propose still reads as giving Redwood too much discretion to file arbitration and avoid immediate injunctive relief. Our GC wants that, in narrowly defined cases, a court may enjoin activity immediately and that such remedies are not waived by arbitration.

That said, we recognize Redwood's concern about jurisdiction shopping. Would you consider this formula instead?

  "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek emergency injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction where irreparable harm is likely. Any party seeking such relief shall: (i) notify the other party and the arbitrator promptly; (ii) use commercially reasonable efforts to limit the scope and duration of the requested relief; and (iii) commence arbitration within thirty (30) days of filing for injunctive relief. If arbitration proceeds, the court shall retain jurisdiction to enforce any interim measures ordered until the arbitrator issues a final award."

I'll escalate if Redwood cannot accept Delaware.

Tom
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Riggins <legal@clearharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jasmine_liu@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines: governing law & emergency relief

Tom — thanks, and understood on Delaware preference. Proposed final compromise from Redwood Legal:

- Governing Law: State of Delaware.
- Dispute Resolution: Binding arbitration (AAA) for all disputes except as set forth below.
- Emergency/Equitable Relief: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent imminent and irreparable harm relating to (a) unauthorized exfiltration of customer data, (b) ongoing theft or misuse of Redwood's models or service, or (c) breaches that present a material security risk. Any party seeking such provisional relief shall: (i) use commercially reasonable efforts to limit scope and duration; (ii) contemporaneously notify the arbitrator and the opposing party; and (iii) commence arbitration within thirty (30) days of seeking provisional relief. The court may retain jurisdiction to enforce interim measures until final arbitration award."

We believe that narrowly enumerating the harms addresses ClearHarbor's desire to preserve emergency relief while limiting forum shopping. If that's acceptable, we'll produce a clean MSA and Order Form for signature.

Aditya Rao
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
